classification.habitat: Open forests, hills and cultivated landscapes
classification.distribution: Widely distributed and cultivated in India and South/Southeast Asia

identification.description: A deciduous tree readily recognized by its characteristic bilobed leaves and showy orchid-like flowers.
identification.whole_plant: Small to medium tree with spreading crown.
identification.leaf: Simple alternate leaves, nearly round with a deep cleft dividing the two lobes, resembling a camel's hoof.
identification.flower: Large showy white, pink or purple flowers with prominent stamens, borne in clusters.
identification.fruit: Flat elongated pod containing several seeds.
identification.seed: Several flattened seeds within the mature pod.
identification.bark: Grey-brown bark, medicinal bark material should be authenticated.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Bauhinia variegata is a widely cultivated medicinal and ornamental tree. Traditional Kanchanara use is part-specific and should not be generalized to all plant preparations.
modern_information.safety_notes: Authenticate bark and avoid unsupervised long-term use of concentrated preparations.

exam_points: Stem bark is the listed useful part

teaching_points: Use the bilobed leaf as a high-yield practical character.
practical_points: Observe leaf cleft, flower colour and pod shape.
